Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1168); Baal, a Phœnician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry):--Baal.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says God kept for himself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal. The Greek name for Baal, used once, in the middle of the argument that God has not cast away his people — there is always a remnant, and it belongs to him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the seven thousand are my comfort in dark days: God always keeps a remnant, and I mean to be counted in it.
